title: The Muscular System
objectiveBasis: Original course objectives aligned to OpenStax sections and the BI 231 muscle checklist. Exam weights are a study blueprint, not instructor-supplied weights.

sections.title: Interactions of Skeletal Muscles, Their Fascicle Arrangement, and Their Lever Systems

objectives.text: Relate attachments to muscle roles in a specified movement, including agonists, antagonists, synergists and fixators.
Compare fascicle arrangements and their effects on force capacity and excursion.
Identify effort, load and fulcrum, classify levers, and explain moment-arm trade-offs.
Recognize location, shape, size, fiber direction, attachment, head-count and action clues in muscle names.
Decode names while distinguishing similarly named muscles, groups and accepted synonyms.

sections.title: Axial Muscles of the Head, Neck, and Back

objectives.text: Locate facial-expression and mastication muscles and explain their main actions and general attachments.
Distinguish extraocular and eyelid muscles and interpret eye actions in a specified gaze position.
Relate tongue and hyoid muscles to shape, position and swallowing using general attachment relationships.
Identify neck and back groups and predict unilateral versus bilateral actions.

sections.title: Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

objectives.text: Identify abdominal-wall layers and relate general attachments to trunk movement and compression.
Explain diaphragm and intercostal contributions to quiet inspiration, quiet expiration and forced breathing.
Distinguish pelvic-diaphragm support, perineal structures and external sphincter functions.

sections.title: Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

objectives.text: Identify scapular positioners and explain their actions and general attachments.
Identify muscles moving the humerus, including rotator-cuff membership, actions and general attachments.
Distinguish elbow flexion/extension from radioulnar pronation/supination using muscle attachments.
Identify wrist and hand muscles, distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic muscles, and relate tendon paths to action.

sections.title: Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

objectives.text: Identify hip muscles, general attachments and contributions to movement and pelvic stability.
Compare quadriceps, hamstrings and other thigh muscles at the hip and knee, including head-specific exceptions.
Identify leg compartments and relate attachments to ankle, foot and toe actions.
Identify intrinsic foot groups/layers and distinguish toe actions and the second-toe reference axis.

sourceCorrections.note: The abdominal wall muscle is rectus abdominis, not rectus femoris. Preserve the lateral wall layers and rectus sheath distinction.
Infraspinatus attaches from scapula to the greater tubercle of the humerus; do not copy the caption that suggests a scapular insertion.
Deltoid arises from clavicle, acromion and scapular spine; trapezius is not a deltoid origin. Infraspinatus and teres minor laterally rotate the humerus.
Supinator and biceps brachii both contribute to supination. The illustrated palm-up entry is correct; conflicting surrounding prose is not used.
Gluteus minimus abducts the hip; pectineus adducts and flexes it. Resolve conflicting movement descriptions before grading.
Only three plantar layers are illustrated, although four layers are described. The dorsal and plantar views represent different sides.
Plantar interossei adduct; dorsal interossei abduct. Abductor hallucis abducts the great toe. Flexor digitorum brevis acts on toes 2–5.
